evals.prompt: Can you show me the tickets assigned to me in Jira that are not Done, ideally as a small table with key, status, priority, and summary? Please don't open the interactive UI.
evals.expected_output: Uses jira issue list with assignee set to $(jira me), excludes Done, requests --plain output with explicit columns, and explains the command/run result.
assertions: Output includes a jira issue list command
Command filters assignee to the current user with $(jira me)
Command excludes Done status or equivalent done category
Command uses --plain or another non-interactive machine-readable output mode
Command selects key/status/priority/summary columns or explains equivalent output

evals.prompt: Create a bug in project PAY titled 'Checkout page hangs on coupon apply'. Body should say: Steps: open checkout, enter SAVE10, click Apply. Expected: discount appears. Actual: spinner never stops. Set priority High, labels checkout and regression.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a Jira write operation, summarizes the intended change, shows a safe jira issue create command using project PAY/type Bug/priority High/labels/body, and asks for confirmation before running unless explicitly told to run now.
assertions: Output treats issue creation as a write operation requiring confirmation
Command uses jira issue create with project PAY and type Bug
Command includes the requested summary, priority High, and both labels
Command preserves the multiline bug body accurately
Command uses --no-input or otherwise avoids unexpected interactive prompting

evals.prompt: I need a quick sprint handoff: list current sprint issues assigned to me, then identify anything high priority or still In Progress. Use Jira CLI and keep it reproducible.
evals.expected_output: Uses jira sprint list --current with assignee filter and plain/raw output, provides a reproducible command, and summarizes high-priority/In Progress items from the results.
assertions: Output includes jira sprint list --current or an equivalent current sprint command
Command filters to the current user with $(jira me)
Command uses --plain/--raw/--csv rather than the interactive explorer
Output requests or includes columns needed to identify priority and status
Response says it will call out high-priority or In Progress issues
